Every number in the claim is there: gaussian_y00_x00 cc_union has loglik 6847.017, 200 coefficients, log_sd_g -35.66, converged=false, against -294.062 for cc_concrete. poisson_y00_x00 cc_union has -197.053 with slope 24.41 and converged=true, against -311.450. gamma_y00_x00 cc_union has +2455.013, converged=false, against -339.040. mechanism: `_design` (src/gaussian_core.jl:388-430) passes the user's data straight to `StatsModels.schema` at :411, `apply_schema` at :419 and `modelcols` at :421. Only the response is narrowed first, by `_coerce_response_column` (:345-359, called at :391). Predictor columns keep their eltype. In StatsModels 0.7.10 (src/schema.jl:200 and :207), `concrete_term` gives ContinuousTerm only for `AbstractVector{<:Number}`. Any other AbstractVector, including Vector{Union{Missing,Float64}}, becomes a CategoricalTerm with DummyCoding, so there is one dummy per distinct value. StatsModels' own `ModelFrame` avoids this because `missing_omit` (src/modelframe.jl:51-67) always narrows with `nonmissingtype`, but DRModels never builds a ModelFrame. No file in src/*.jl calls nonmissingtype, disallowmissing or missing_omit. drm_listwise has the same gap at src/missing_data.jl:111: `ndropped == 0 && return cols` returns the columns un-narrowed. Yet its own comment at :112-117 says the `identity.` narrowing on line 118 is needed because "an un-narrowed `Union{Missing,…}` column would still break the fitter's numeric path". The narrowing is applied only on the branch that drops rows. Its docstring says "If no rows are dropped the input columns are returned unchanged". The test (B2) in test/test_missing_listwise.jl only uses Vector{Float64}, so the Union case with no drops is never tested. Nothing in the docs, NEWS or tests says Union eltypes are intended to mean categorical. The unconditional narrowing is the evident intent.

corrections:
The claim is accurate. Refinements:
(a) The StatsModels version is 0.7.10. The line references are schema.jl:200/207 at that version, and gaussian_core.jl:411/419/421 at the pin.
(b) Only predictor columns are affected, on the mu formula and also on sigma (sigma ~ x with a Union x gave 60 sigma coefficients). A Union response is narrowed by _coerce_response_column. In listwise_union the Union y and g are harmless; x causes the problem.
(c) The converged flag only partly warns. It was false for Gaussian and Gamma. For Poisson it was true in t5 (poisson_y00_x00, poisson_y20_x20) and false in my synthetic run. So "converged=TRUE" holds for those t5 cells but not for Poisson in general.
(d) Confounder in reproductions: at the pin, DrmFormula.schema_cache is first-write-wins, and is being removed in #1086. If the same bf object is fitted on Float64 data first, a later fit on Union data silently reuses the continuous schema and looks correct. The reverse also happens: a bf first fitted on Union data poisoned a later Float64 fit (+2073.05, 60 coefficients). A Union x with a real missing then reports "predict: column `x` in `newdata` contains `missing`". Every reproduction must build a fresh bf() per fit. The t5 probe does: one process per cell and F() called fresh.
(e) The DataFrames triggers come from reading, not running. DataFrames is not in the project environment. The underlying fact is plain Julia: boolean-mask indexing (`xu[mask]`, `df[completecases(df), :]`, `filter`) keeps the Union eltype, while `dropmissing` narrows by default.
(f) The suggested fix scope for the #1089 comment is to narrow every model column with `nonmissingtype` after the missing check, as StatsModels.missing_omit does. Do it in drm or _design, and remove the early return at missing_data.jl:111 (or narrow there too). Add a test for a Union column with nothing missing. If the maintainers would rather keep #1089 to "missing present → drop or error", file this as its own issue instead, because it is a silent wrong result, not a loud error.
realistic_input: A continuous predictor column whose eltype is Union{Missing,Float64} but which holds no missing values. Typical sources: CSV.read on a file with NA in x, followed by `df[completecases(df), :]`, `filter` or `subset` (all keep the eltype); `allowmissing!`; or the package's own drm_listwise() when no rows need dropping (missing_data.jl:111). Users coming from GLM or MixedModels expect this to work, because StatsModels.ModelFrame narrows such columns and treats them as continuous.

corrections:
1. Poisson and Gamma numbers: those in the claim come from marginal=:Laplace. The probe script sets this at /home/user/drmTMB/sweep-oct16/t5/julia/probe_union.jl:36. The default marginal is :LA (src/poisson.jl:133, src/gamma.jl:46), and there:

- Gamma is worse than the claim says: a silent saturated fit with converged=TRUE (loglik +2197.81, against -339.01 with Float64 x).

2. Not always meaningless: the fit is obviously broken only when x has nearly one distinct value per row. With a few distinct values it looks plausible and reports converged=true: rounded x gave 6, 9 and 7 coefficients with loglik within about 1.7 of the correct fit. That is the more dangerous form.

3. Not specific to Missing: Vector{Any} and Vector{Union{Nothing,Float64}} behave the same way. Vector{Real}, Float32 and a Union response are fine. A Union x that really contains missing values fails with "KeyError: key missing not found" instead.

4. Realistic triggers: I confirmed by running df[completecases(df), :], subset and filter. I did not test allowmissing!; it would yield the same column eltype as the Union vectors I did test. dropmissing narrows the column and is safe.

5. Line references: the schema call is at gaussian_core.jl:411 and modelcols at :421. The un-narrowed pass-through is at :391-393, where only the response is coerced. The StatsModels dispatch is at schema.jl:200 and :207-208.

6. Confound for anyone reproducing this: the Gaussian fitter caches the schema on the formula object, in `DrmFormula.schema_cache` (gaussian_core.jl:42, filled at :411-412), and never resets it between fits. Reusing one bf() across fits therefore:
- can mask this bug: Float64 first, then Union, gives 2 coefs and -294.061721;
- can carry it into clean data: Union rounded first, then plain Float64 rounded x, gives 6 coefs;
- can raise a misleading "predict: `newdata` ..." error at fit time.

Use a fresh bf() for every fit when reproducing. This coupling is tracked by open #1086.
realistic_input: The common case: a CSV is read into a DataFrame and a numeric covariate has some NA, so the column is typed Union{Missing,Float64}. The user then removes incomplete rows with df[completecases(df), :], subset(df, :x => ByRow(!ismissing)) or filter, which keep the Union eltype, and calls drm(bf(@formula(y ~ x + (1|g)), @formula(sigma ~ 1)), Gaussian(); data = df). Calling drm_listwise on data that is already complete hits the same bug, as does building data as Union{Missing,Float64} vectors the way the package docs do (docs/src/reference/model-specification.md:83-84) when no value happens to be missing. A low-cardinality numeric covariate such as dose 0-3 or a year index is silently fitted as a factor, the fit reports converged=true, and the loglik looks plausible.

mechanism:
At the pin, nothing on the formula path checks that predictors are finite.

- StatsModels 0.7.10, schema.jl:200-204, builds a ContinuousTerm from mean/var/min/max with no NaN check. terms.jl:508 `modelcols(t::ContinuousTerm, d) = copy.(d[t.sym])` copies NaN or Inf into the design matrix.
- DRModels `_design` (src/gaussian_core.jl:388-432) only masks the response. `_fit_observed_response_rows` (gaussian_core.jl:1317-1331) drops rows with a NaN or missing response only.
- Two in-code statements are false for this input:
  - gaussian_core.jl:1324: "Predictor missingness still errors."
  - The drm_listwise docstring, src/missing_data.jl:57-58: a NaN predictor "makes `drm` error".

Poisson (1|g) path:
- poisson.jl:162 builds Xμ; poisson.jl:241-242 calls `_fit_poisson_ranef`.
- The likelihood at poisson.jl:323 uses `clamp(η,-30,30)`, which passes NaN through.
- In src/adaptive_ghq.jl the per-group mode search gives up on a non-finite value. Newton stops at :234, and the Cholesky fails at :236-237 and :252-253. Line :267 then returns `convert(T,-Inf)` for any group that contains a NaN row, so nll(θ0) = +Inf.
- Optim 1.13.3 (multivariate/optimize/optimize.jl:26-30, `initial_convergence`) stops before the first iteration when the objective is not finite. The minimizer is therefore θ0 (poisson.jl:327-329: log(mean y), slope 0, log σ_b = log 0.5).
- poisson.jl:331 `drm_optim_converged` gives false.
- poisson.jl:347 builds the vcov from a ForwardDiff Hessian. The -Inf groups carry zero derivative terms, so the Hessian comes from the finite groups only and is positive definite. That is why the SEs are finite and coeftable looks normal.

Gaussian (1|g): gaussian_ranef.jl:612 calls `_vcov_from_hessian`, and src/vcov_guard.jl:83 runs `eigvals` on the NaN Hessian. LAPACK's `chkuplofinite` then throws, after the optimizer has run, not when the input is read. Poisson fixed-effects and :VA fail the same way (poisson.jl:518 to vcov_guard.jl:83).

Gamma: gamma.jl:155-156 calls `Distributions.Gamma(α, μ/α)` with μ = exp(clamp(NaN)) = NaN, and Distributions' `check_args` throws DomainError.

Binomial and Student report the raw `fit.converged=true`. I did not trace why. gamma.jl:171 uses plain `Optim.converged(res)`, which suggests some routes do not go through `drm_optim_converged`.

PR #1045 adds `_require_finite_predictor_columns` and `_require_finite_inputs` inside `_design`, restricted to rows with an observed response (PR gaussian_core.jl:429, :468), so every route that goes through `_design` is covered.

mechanism:
The grouping column never goes through the StatsModels missing/levels path, and the label mapper has no missing check.

1. _split_ranef (src/gaussian_ranef.jl:137-138) moves every `(lhs | g)` term out of the fixed RHS into `re` and keeps only the grouping symbol. So g never reaches _design's schema/modelcols (src/gaussian_core.jl:388-428). For an ordinary fixed term, StatsModels builds categorical levels with DataAPI.levels, which skips missing ($JULIA_DEPOT_PATH/packages/StatsModels/OasXV/src/schema.jl:207-213), and modelcols then throws KeyError. I observed that KeyError with y ~ x + g.

2. Each route reads the raw column with getproperty(data, grp) and calls _group_index (src/gaussian_ranef.jl:212-219). That function builds `Dict{eltype(labels),Int}()` at :213 and assigns codes with `get!(lvl, l, length(lvl)+1)` at :216. Dict keys compare with isequal, so `missing` (and NaN) become ordinary keys: one pooled extra level, G=26.

Call sites I hit:
- gaussian_core.jl: 1192 (single (1|g)), 1183 (1+x|g), 1200 (crossed), 990 (mu+sigma random effects), 999 (sigma random effect).
- poisson.jl:226 and :220; gamma.jl:123 and :116.
- ordinary_laplace.jl:104 (marginal=:Laplace).
- The same pattern is in binomial/negbinomial/student/lognormal/beta/tweedie/cumulative.

3. The response-missing pre-filter _fit_observed_response_rows (gaussian_core.jl:1317-1331) masks only the response, so it does not catch this.

Other routes already guard this case: temporal.jl:242-244, gaussian_lss.jl:298-299 (phylo LSS) and inference.jl:1969 (LSS bootstrap) all throw ArgumentError on missing labels.
